method: Built-in image_gen tool; original in-game sprites used as visual references.

ships.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: five-view orthographic spaceship reference sheet for building a textured 3D game model. Input image 1 is the existing game's pirate ship sprite: preserve its recognizable silhouette, key hardware and worn surface palette while resolving all sides into one coherent solid craft. Create ONE professional landscape 3:2 reference sheet at high resolution, not a scene. Pure white background, soft neutral studio lighting, evenly readable dark surfaces, no ground shadows or glow obscuring geometry. Five precisely orthographic views of the SAME ship, consistent geometry and details across views: TOP and BOTTOM large and vertically aligned side by side across the left two-thirds, noses pointing UP; right third stacks FRONT, BACK and SIDE, with SIDE nose pointing LEFT. Each view fully in frame, isolated with generous white gaps and small black labels exactly 'TOP', 'BOTTOM', 'FRONT', 'BACK', 'SIDE'. Small title at top. Equal top/bottom scale and matching nose, wings and engine locations. Front/back correspond correctly to top silhouette. Side shows real hull thickness. No perspective beauty view, no extra ships, no diagrams or dimensions or tiny annotations, no logos or watermark. High quality hard-surface science fiction art with physically legible paneling; details should suit a low-polygon mesh with painted textures. Strong, distinct silhouette. Underside is fully designed and as detailed as the top: armored keel, recessed maintenance panels, weapon/engine connections. No pure black featureless bottom. Engines glow warm amber inside RECESSED nozzle mouths, no long exhaust flames. Title: 'PRIVATEER RAIDER'. Faithfully develop the input's compact, long narrow pointed armored nose, midship raised dark-glass canopy, chunky shoulders, short asymmetric-looking patched swept wings, two forward side-mounted paired gun barrels, and THREE exposed cylindrical engines side-by-side across the stern. Keep three engines, the middle slightly farther back. Blackened gunmetal, layered salvaged gray plating, burnt orange and worn mustard-yellow wing panels with chipped edges, dull bronze mechanical piping. The port wing's orange patch and starboard wing's yellow patch are distinct. Mostly bilaterally symmetric hull geometry, asymmetry in salvage plates and paint only. Low armored cockpit and real underslung machinery; no giant fins, no skull motif, no organic parts.

ships.correction: Edit this spaceship modeling reference sheet. Keep the title and BOTH large TOP and BOTTOM drawings pixel-for-pixel in shape, position, scale, panel details, colors and layout. Replace ONLY the three smaller right-hand drawings labeled FRONT, BACK and SIDE. They must be true engineering ORTHOGRAPHIC projections of this SAME very low, flat ship, not views from above and not three-quarter views. FRONT: look precisely down the ship's long axis from the nose, with NO foreshortened fuselage extending upwards or backwards; it appears as a thin wide wing/central-body cross-section, with the central nose/canopy seen end-on and two small dorsal guns. BACK: look precisely down the long axis from directly behind at zero elevation, showing a thin wide flat wing cross-section, a low central body and the THREE round warm orange exhausts in one row. The long nose must be COMPLETELY OCCLUDED by the stern in the BACK view. SIDE: true port profile seen exactly perpendicular to the long axis at zero elevation, nose LEFT; the nearer wing is seen only edge-on, do not show its large triangular top surface or a second wing behind it. The side is long and low with a raised slim spine. In all three right views the ship height is about 15 percent of its total width and just 8 percent of its total length. Use clean white background and retain the current labels. Match battered gunmetal, orange stripes and riveted plating. Preserve all five views and entire sheet. These drawings are for accurate 3D reconstruction; no perspective distortion.
